rows.whatWasWrong: Two independent check-box defects, both visible on a filing, both confirmed against the pinned sources and against the sources' own page-drawing operators.

defectOne.class: ink this packet ADDED -- pdf-lib synthesized widget border
defectOne.cause: Each of these widgets ships an /AP /N carrying an /On state ONLY -- a ZapfDingbats check mark inside a clip, no box. Their /AS is /Off. Under ISO 32000-1 12.5.5 a state absent from /AP /N is drawn as nothing; pdf-lib instead synthesizes `0 0 0 RG / 0 w / [] 0 d / 0 0 m ... h / S` at the widget /Rect and flatten stamps it. The official page already prints its own box at each of those rectangles, so the stamp lands as a second, thickened outline over the court's.
defectOne.measuredAt600dpi: 136 added dark pixels at ORDER Checkbox1, 136 and 80 at the two PETITION Checkbox2 widgets, every one of them on the left and right edges of the printed box. 0 removed.
defectOne.remedy: REMOVE -- suppressSynthesizedAppearances, which installs the empty appearance the source's silence means.

defectTwo.class: ink this packet UNCOVERED -- the court's own white mask stripped off
defectTwo.cause: These two are the Yes/No election under the printed question that ends '...due been paid?'. The petition's own page content stream draws a SMALLER box at each -- `0.72 w 1 J / 466.68 271.62 -9.3 -9.3 re / S` and the same at 538.68 -- and the widget's /Off appearance paints `1 g` over it and strokes a larger one, so the control reads as ONE hollow box, which is what a conforming viewer and the court's own PDF show. stripOpaqueBackgroundPaint removes any leading fill at grey >= 0.9 covering the widget, so it removed this white one, and the printed 9.3 x 9.3pt box reappeared INSIDE the widget's 15.03 x 12.80pt box.
defectTwo.measuredAt600dpi: 1,262 added dark pixels across the two widgets -- measured as rectangles at x 457.92-466.92 y 262.08-271.80 and x 529.12-538.96 y 261.96-271.32, which are the page's own two drawn rectangles to within antialiasing. Two concentric outlines at each of the two Yes/No controls on a filing.
defectTwo.remedy: RESTORE -- preserveUnwrittenSelectionBackgrounds, which keeps the source's authored blank-state paint on a selection this run did not write. /MK /BG is still removed, so no background the form did not itself author is requested.
defectTwo.whyThisIsTheValuableHalf: The ledger classed both of these as invented. Removing them would have deleted the court's own check-box stroke from the fee question on a Rule 790 petition.

sameMechanismElsewhereOnThisHost.question: Whether the Pennsylvania unaccounted ink is one mechanism across the whole host, and which families it reaches.
sameMechanismElsewhereOnThisHost.answer: It is NOT one mechanism, and the two mechanisms have different reaches.
sameMechanismElsewhereOnThisHost.mechanismA: pdf-lib synthesizing an appearance for a check box whose current /AS state has no /AP /N entry. This is a property of the FORM, not of the family: it reaches any family that flattens PA-RCRIM-P-790-ORDER (Checkbox1/2/3) or PA-RCRIM-P-790-PETITION (both Checkbox2 widgets) through a finalizer call that does not pass suppressSynthesizedAppearances.
sameMechanismElsewhereOnThisHost.mechanismB: stripOpaqueBackgroundPaint removing a WHITE `1 g` widget background that the form uses as a mask over its own printed art. On these sources it is confined to the two `Check Box1` widgets on PA-RCRIM-P-790-PETITION, because they are the only widgets whose /Off appearance masks a rectangle the page itself draws.
sameMechanismElsewhereOnThisHost.whatThisDoesAndDoesNotSayAboutOtherFamil: Any family binding either of these two PA forms and flattening without those options will carry the same ink, because the cause is in the source form and the shared default. That is a prediction about a form, exactly the kind of static prediction BORDER_COHORT_REMEDIATION.json warns must be measured on delivered bytes before it is acted on -- FIX121 measured such a prediction on New Jersey and found it did not hold. It should be checked per family against that family's own delivered fixtures, and this lane checked none but its own.
sameMechanismElsewhereOnThisHost.pa490AndPa790Nonconviction: Recorded as cleared by the source accounting -- every stroke on them the form's own. This lane's reading does not contradict that and does not extend it: neither family was claimed or read. Note only that 'every stroke matches a source stream' and 'the page is right' are different statements, and that mechanism B produces a page defect while leaving every delivered stroke derived from the source.
sameMechanismElsewhereOnThisHost.recommendation: Dispatch per family, on that family's delivered bytes, with the directional raster read in both directions. Do not treat this row as authority to turn the options on in another family's builder.
